page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an Arm-based virtual server from the Cost Optimized family, provisioned through QEMU virtualization. The instance features an 8-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the arm64 architecture, configured with 8 vCPUs under a shared allocation model with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is set at 16.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 1.95 GB per core. Bundled local storage includes a 160 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results reflect the shared Arm architecture profile. The instance delivers average multi-core execution in stress-ng (14,164.78) and Geekbench multi-core (5,619.0), with Clang software compilation reaching 8,251.0. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,029.0 and PassMark CPU score of 6,028.96. Memory read bandwidth registers at 75.87 GB/sec for uncached 256MB blocks, though PassMark memory performance remains modest at 1,636.33. Data throughput benchmarks demonstrate solid baseline results, with Redis SET handling 9.74 million operations per second and static web serving achieving 7.92 GB/sec. Machine learning capabilities are restricted; small model (135M) generation operates at 84.71 tokens per second, but 7B model generation drops to 5.66 tokens per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high core density yields strong cost efficiency for scale-out parallel tasks that do not depend on x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. The presence of fast local NVMe storage benefits disk-bound read/write patterns. Hetzner Cloud cax31 is best suited for multi-threaded software compilation, containerized microservices, web serving, background processing queues, and lightweight database workloads.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64 compute-oriented instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.0 GHz on a shared allocation model. The server provides 16.0 GB of RAM, a 1:2 core-to-memory distribution, and 160 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-threaded capabilities, achieving 14,164.78 in stress-ng multi-core, 8,251.0 in Clang software compilation, and 9.74 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded throughput and memory-heavy execution show lower efficiency, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,029.0 and PassMark CPU at 6,028.96. Given its high core count and bundled NVMe disk at a shared-resource tier, the instance delivers dependable cost efficiency for parallelized application workloads, web serving, CI/CD code builds, and distributed application runtimes.
